editing_rules: Cut every 1.5-3 seconds maximum - hyper-fast transitions
Use jump cuts within same scene to compress time and add energy
Start with immediate action - no intros or fades
Include at least one 'payoff' or punchline moment (mishap, reveal, reaction)
Show process quickly: setup (2-3 clips) → action (3-4 clips) → result/reaction (1-2 clips)
Keep total duration 20-60 seconds for shorts format
Add speed ramps on mundane tasks (1.2-1.5x) to maintain momentum
Use match cuts between similar actions for rhythm
Include relatable 'struggle' or 'comedy of errors' moments
End on reaction shot, reveal, or comedic beat - no fade outs

Color: Natural/warm domestic lighting - no color grading. Slightly saturated consumer camera look. Indoor warm tones (yellows, oranges) or natural outdoor light. Authentic, unfiltered, smartphone-native colors.
Texture: Clean digital - minimal to no grain. Smartphone camera aesthetic. Slightly soft focus acceptable. Prioritize clarity over film texture.

Framing: Vertical 9:16 with subject centered. Medium-close shots dominate. Handheld, slightly shaky cam for authenticity. Blurred side panels when repurposing horizontal footage. Eye-level or slightly above. Show hands/action in frame with face.

On-screen text: Bold sans-serif, white with black stroke or solid color background. Positioned top-third or bottom-third. Emoji-heavy. Text appears for 1-2 seconds max, synced to action. Minimal animation - pop-in or simple fade.
avoid: Slow motion (unless for comedic payoff, max 1 second)
Complex transitions (wipes, spins, etc.) - stick to cuts
Multiple storylines - one simple narrative arc only
pacing: Frenetic and relentless. Average shot length 1.5-2.5 seconds. Constant forward momentum with no breathing room. Prioritize watch-through rate over artistic timing. Every cut must advance the micro-narrative or add comedic/emotional value.
notes: These vlogs thrive on authenticity, relatability, and compression. The viewer should feel like they're experiencing a full 'day moment' in under a minute. Humor comes from real mishaps, not scripted gags. Mobile-first vertical framing dominates.
